Good morning to the regulars and welcome to anyone who found this thread through the search page. I have fixed bicycles in a rented garage behind the bakery for about six years, and this spring I finally have enough space to take on more work, so here is how the workshop runs from now on. I service every kind of bike that comes through the door, from children's first bikes to heavy cargo frames, but I specialise in steel touring bikes and in the hub gears that most shops no longer want to open. A standard service covers cleaning the drivetrain, truing both wheels, adjusting the brakes and gears, and checking every bolt with a torque wrench. A full overhaul adds new cables and housing, fresh grease in the bearings and a written report on anything that will need attention within the year. Prices are posted on the board inside the door and they include the labour but not the parts, because parts vary so much between models. If you bring your own parts I will fit them, but I cannot promise anything about parts I did not choose. Most repairs are ready within three days; wheel builds take about a week because I let the spokes settle before the final tension. I keep a waiting list for the busy months, usually from April to June, and I send a text message the day before your slot so you can bring the bike in the morning. Please remove bags, lights and child seats before you drop the bike off, since I do not want to be responsible for anything that is not bolted on. Electric bikes are welcome for mechanical work, but I do not open batteries or motors, and I will say so before I start. I also run a small evening class on the first Wednesday of each month, where you can learn to fix a puncture, adjust your brakes and look after your chain. The class is free for anyone who has had a service here in the last year and costs a small fee otherwise, which goes towards tools for the shared bench. Second hand bikes are sometimes for sale when owners leave them with me to sell; each one is checked and serviced first, and I list them on this thread with honest photos. I do not buy stolen bikes, and I ask for a frame number and a receipt or a reasonable story before I take one in. If you think a bike on my list belongs to you, come and talk to me and bring whatever proof you have. Payment is by card or cash at collection, and regulars can open a tab for small jobs if they settle it at the end of the month. I close for two weeks every August and between Christmas and the new year, and I post the dates here well in advance. Thank you to everyone who has recommended the workshop to friends; almost all of my new customers come that way. Ride safely, pump up your tyres every week, and bring the bike in before a small noise turns into a large bill.
